status: FROZEN before any of the forecasts it scores existed: the test-year forecasts of control2000 and tailC2000, and the 16-member validation forecasts. The SHA-256 of this file is recorded in the commit that froze it.
title: Does fine-tuning with extra weight on precipitation, followed by calibration, beat the calibrated control on heavy rain?
origin: Exploratory analysis on the validation period (scripts/hits_and_calibration.py, 2026-10-06) found variant C worse than control2000 on raw heavy-rain scores through false alarms, yet better after week-out isotonic calibration: Brier at 10 mm -9 percent (interval excluding zero), at 20 mm -6 percent (interval touching zero), with a higher ROC area. Found after looking, on 61 days of one season; this plan tests it on data where neither model's calibration has been examined and C has never been scored.

models.control2000: finetune.yaml at step 2000 of the 3 000-step schedule: ~/bris-models/control/control-step002000_inference.ckpt
models.tailC2000: finetune_tail_c at step 2000 of the same schedule: ~/bris-models/tailC2000/tailC2000-step002000_inference.ckpt

test.forecasts: bris/slurm/bris_forecast.sbatch, 4 members, 7 lead times; 2025-08-01..2025-09-07 from the year2 datasets and 2025-09-08..2026-09-06 from year1, as the main evaluation
test.cases: strict common cases of control2000, tailC2000 and MEPS (~/bris-runs/meps/precipitation_daily.npz) at screened gauges (~/bris-runs/observations, quality code 4 or better, within 5 km), as the main evaluation
test.event: gauge 06-06 UTC total above the threshold
test.probability: share of the 4 members above the threshold

calibration.primary: isotonic regression of the event on the probability, per model and threshold, leave-one-calendar-month-out within the test period: every month is calibrated with a map fitted on all the other months (hits_and_calibration.py --cv month)
calibration.secondary: isotonic maps fitted on the validation period (2025-04-01..2025-07-31, every second day; ~/bris-runs/round3/hits-calibration-cases.npz) and applied unchanged to the test period, fully out of sample (--fit-cache)

primary_endpoint.measure: Brier score at 20 mm per day after primary calibration, tailC2000 minus control2000
primary_endpoint.uncertainty: paired block bootstrap, seven-day calendar blocks, 5000 replicates
primary_endpoint.positive_if: the upper 95 percent bound is below 0
primary_endpoint.negative_if: the lower 95 percent bound is above 0

secondary_reported: raw (uncalibrated) Brier, ROC area, hits and false alarms with yes at half and at a quarter of the members, twCRPS split into event and non-event days

sample_size_check.question: Is C's advantage after calibration a sample-size effect of four members (a wetter model leaves fewer cases at probability 0), or does it hold with sixteen?
sample_size_check.forecasts: control2000 and tailC2000 with 16 members on the validation days (every second day 2025-04-01..2025-07-31)
sample_size_check.reported: week-out calibrated Brier and ROC area at 10 and 20 mm for 16 members against the same for 4; the C minus control difference with both
sample_size_check.reading: the advantage is a sample-size effect if it disappears with 16 members; real if it remains

neighbourhood_prediction.registered: From scripts/neighbourhood_probability.py on the 4-member validation forecasts (~/bris-runs/neighbourhood/control2000-tailC2000.json), extrapolated with Brier(m) = Brier(inf) + b/m. At 20 mm, 16 members at the gauge cell: control2000 0.0153 (4 members 0.01726, infinite 0.01469), tailC2000 0.0154 (0.01791, 0.01449). The best 4-member neighbourhood of control2000 scored 0.0162 (25 km).
neighbourhood_prediction.reading: if 16 members at the gauge cell reach about the extrapolated score and beat the best 4-member neighbourhood, the neighbourhood gain was sample size, as the extrapolation said

not_claimed: Passing would show that weighting precipitation in fine-tuning adds information that calibration can use, at 2000 steps, on one season-spanning year, from one training run per arm. It would not show the same for a full-length run or another seed; those would be the next tests.
